Write the main text for my sales page. I'm a bookkeeper and I work only with hair and nail salons. I do monthly books, payroll for up to 10 staff, and sales tax filing.

What's true:
- I have 31 salon clients. 2 left last year, both because they sold their salons.
- I charge $199 a month. Until January it was $149, and I raised it for everyone, including existing clients.
- I close each month's books by the 10th of the next month. I missed that date 3 times last year.
- Last tax season, 9 of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because the books came in clean. One said she saved $800.
- I'm one person. I don't answer the phone on Sundays or Mondays.
- The first call is free and takes 20 minutes.

Keep it to about 350 words, with a button at the end to book the call.

Before I write, a few questions. Each answer would change what the page says.

1. **Who's reading it?** Is it mostly salon owners doing their own books, or owners switching from another bookkeeper? That changes what the page leads with: getting hours back, or better service than they get now.

2. **The 3 missed closes.** I plan to put these on the page, because a reader who hears about them later will doubt everything else. What happened those times? How late were the books, and did you tell the client ahead of time? If you now do something to prevent it or to warn clients early, that's the best answer to the obvious worry that you're only one person.

3. **The price rise.** It's November 2026, so "last year" means 2025 and the raise to $199 came after it. Has any client left since the raise? If none have, that's a strong point for the page. Also, what happens for a salon with more than 10 staff, or one that needs catch-up work on past months?

4. **Being reachable.** Apart from Sundays and Mondays, how do clients reach you (phone, text, email) and how quickly do you usually reply? Owners will ask "what if you're sick or on vacation?" Do you have an answer you can stand behind?

5. **Why salons.** What's your background with salons? Did you work in one, own one, or have you just done this for years? How many years? Also, what salon-specific things do you handle that a general bookkeeper gets wrong (tips, booth rent vs. commission staff, retail product sales tax)? This shows the reader you know their world.

6. **Terms and names.** Is there a contract or minimum term, or can clients cancel any month? What should the page call you or your business? Anything else on this list a prospect will find out anyway, like a setup fee or a slow onboarding?

When I write it, the $800 will stay one client's result and the accountant savings will be what 9 of your 31 clients told you. That way the page doesn't promise savings to everyone.

1. I don't know, I haven't tracked that.

2. I don't have the details on those three. But since January, if I miss the 10th, that month's fee is free.

3. I don't know offhand if anyone's left since the raise. I raised it because I added payroll for up to 10 staff, which I didn't do before. I don't know what I'd do for more than 10 staff or for catch-up work.

4. I don't know what to say on that, and I don't have a sick or vacation plan I can stand behind.

5. I managed a hair salon for 6 years before I became a bookkeeper. I'm not sure what else to list.

6. There's no contract. Clients can stop with 30 days' notice. I'm Carla Benson, and the business is Chair and Ledger. A few other things they'll find out: I don't do income tax returns. Their own accountant or tax preparer keeps doing those and gets clean books from me. I can only take about 5 new clients this year. The button goes to my calendar, and calls are Tuesday to Saturday.

<final_document>
# Bookkeeping for hair and nail salons, from someone who ran one

I'm Carla Benson. I managed a hair salon for six years before I became a bookkeeper. Now I work only with salons. Chair and Ledger keeps the books for 31 hair and nail salons.

## What you get for $199 a month

- Your books closed every month, by the 10th of the following month
- Payroll for up to 10 staff
- Your sales tax filed

There's no contract. If you want to stop, give me 30 days' notice.

## Clean books cost less at tax time

I don't do income tax returns. Your accountant or tax preparer keeps doing those, and they get finished books from me to work from. Last tax season, 9 of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because the books came in clean. One owner said she saved $800. I can't promise you'll save that much. What I can promise is that your accountant starts from finished books.

## The 10th, and what happens if I miss it

I'm one person, so here's the honest record: last year I missed the 10th three times. Since January, if your books aren't closed by the 10th, you don't pay for that month.

## About the price

Until January I charged $149. When I added payroll, I raised the price to $199 for every client, including the ones I already had.

## Who stays

Two clients left last year. Both had sold their salons.

## Before you call

I don't answer the phone on Sundays or Mondays. I can take about five new clients this year.

The first call is free and takes 20 minutes. We'll talk about your salon, and you can decide whether I'm the right fit. Calls run Tuesday to Saturday.

**[Book your free 20-minute call]**
</final_document>

It's about 320 words, and I used every fact you gave me, including the three missed closes, the price rise and the fact that you don't do income tax returns. Each one sits next to the fact that answers it: the free month, payroll being added, and their accountant keeping the tax work.

A few choices to check:

- **"About five new clients this year."** It's mid-November, so "this year" leaves only about six weeks. If you meant 2027, change that line.
- **Things I left off on purpose:** salons with more than 10 staff, catch-up work and cover when you're sick or away. You don't have an answer yet for any of these, so the page doesn't promise one. Expect them to come up on calls.
- **Salon-specific details.** If there are things you handle that a general bookkeeper gets wrong, adding one or two concrete ones under your six years as a manager would make that section stronger. I didn't guess at them.
